subject: general
question: Pipe P can fill (2)/(9) part of a tank in 20 hours, and pipe Q can fill (5)/(9) part of the same tank in 10 hours. Both P and Q were kept open for 3 hours, then both were closed. Pipe R alone was then opened and it emptied the water in the tank in 8 hours. Pipes P, Q and R together can fill the empty tank in:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time for **P** = 20 × (9/2) = 90 hours; Time for **Q** = 10 × (9/5) = 18 hours.

Let Total Work (LCM of 90, 18) = 90 units ⇒ Efficiencies: **P** = 1, **Q** = 5.

Work done in 3 hours = (1 + 5) × 3 = 18 units. Efficiency of **R** = 18/8 = 2.25 (emptying).

Combined Efficiency (P + Q − R) = 1 + 5 − 2.25 = 3.75 units/hr.

Time required = 90 ÷ 3.75 = 24 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 **Pipe**
 **Total Time (Full Tank)**
 **Total Work**

 **P**
 20 × (9/2) = 90 hr
 90 units
 90 ÷ 90 = 1

 **Q**
 10 × (9/5) = 18 hr
 90 ÷ 18 = 5

⇒ Water filled by **P** and **Q** in 3 hours = (1 + 5) × 3 = 18 units.

⇒ Efficiency of pipe **R** (emptying) = Water filled ÷ Time taken = 18 ÷ 8 = 2.25 units/hr.

⇒ Combined efficiency of **P**, **Q**, and **R** = EffP + EffQ − EffR

⇒ Combined efficiency = 1 + 5 − 2.25 = 3.75 units/hr.

⇒ Time to fill the empty tank together = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time = 90 ÷ 3.75 = 24 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Work Concept

If a fraction 1/x of a tank is filled in 't' hours, the full tank is filled in (t × x) hours.

Pipes and Cisterns efficiency

Filling pipes have **positive efficiency**, while emptying/outlet pipes have **negative efficiency**.

Time formula

Time taken = Total Capacity ÷ Net Efficiency of all active pipes.</p
